chapter: Mandeville, Bunk Johnson and society banquets
title: Bunk's playing in the 1940s versus the 1920s
summary: George says Bunk played far better before losing his teeth, with more volume, range and execution.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Yeah, go ahead. I'll get that in my life. Yeah. Now Bunk, his records and his playing during the 40s, how did they compare with the way he played in the 20s?
Well, they didn't compare at all. Bunk played fine on up until Bunk lost his teeth.
Well, he was much better. I know that for a fact, because I played the last jobs with Bunk, and Bunk had his teeth, so I know that for a fact.

Because after Evan Thomas got killed, Bunk taking the job over, we had a couple of jobs to play, and we only used one trumpet. The Bunk was playing fine, but after he lost his teeth and had laid off for that many years, and ten years made him ten years older. That would make some difference. That would make a lot of difference.
Well, the first place, his muscles wasn't as strong, I can say that for one thing. And then with his age, and then with the false teeth, that pressure. That had a lot to do with it.
Did false teeth bother you much on clarinet?
No way, no way, no way, no way, no way.
Did Bunk play louder or softer in the 20s?
He played louder, he played louder, yeah.
Did he ever play very loud?
Definitely louder than he played. Did he have more range or less range? Well, he had more range. More range and he had more execution. It was more fast and more flexible.
